brief: 6 books that quietly changed how I run a company. Why each one mattered.

slots.headline: Six books that quietly changed how I run a company

slots.title: Know Your Time
slots.body: Drucker taught me that effectiveness is a discipline, not a personality. Tracking time ruthlessly revealed where my attention actually went. It changed every hiring and meeting decision.

slots.title: Intent, Not Permission
slots.body: Marquet’s leader-leader model replaced my instinct to approve every move. Pushing authority to the information created a faster, more engaged team.

slots.title: Measure Output
slots.body: Grove reframed management as a production process. Focusing on output, not activity, forced me to build systems that scale without my daily presence.

slots.title: Embrace The Struggle
slots.body: Horowitz made peace with the loneliness of leadership. His lens on peacetime versus wartime CEOs prepared me to adapt culture when survival is at stake.

slots.title: Lead With Vulnerability
slots.body: Brown’s research on shame and courage rewired how I give feedback. Creating psychological safety turned out to be the highest-leverage investment in performance.

slots.title: See The System
slots.body: Meadows shifted my focus from isolated fixes to feedback loops. Understanding delays and bottlenecks helped me stop solving the same problem twice.

slots.headline: Build Your Leadership Library
slots.body: Reply with the title that shaped how you lead. I am always hunting for the next quiet revolution.
